newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan parliament adopts telecoms liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan parliament adopts telecoms liberalisation.

text.p: The Moroccan parliament adopted on Sunday a law on the liberalisation of telecommunications sector, including its GSM mobile phone network, a parliamentary spokesman said.
"The Moroccan parliament adopted the (telecommunications) law by a majority of 62 votes, 43 abstaining and with nobody voting against," the spokesman told Reuters.
The 43 who abstained were all members of the opposition Koutla group (democratic bloc), he said.
Led by the old-guard Istiqlal party, the Koutla is composed of four parties which hold together 125 seats out of a total 333.

Morocco plans to split the state-owned Office National des Telecommunications (ONPT) utility into two enterprises called Ittissalat al-Maghrib and Barid al-Maghrib, handling respectively telecommunications and postal services.
Privatisation will first target GSM phones.
South Korean giant Daewoo, the U.S. AT&T and French Alcatel companies have all closely followed the moves towards telecoms liberalisation, a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
Daewoo has said it would invest up to 1.0 billion dirhams ($105 million) in the GSM mobile telephone network in Morocco after its privatisation, the broker added.
Morocco with a population of 27 million people has only four telephone lines per 100 people and 30,000 GSM subscribers.
